options.content:
### etcd Fsync Performance Dashboard

Disk-level etcd analysis beyond P99 — covering latency distribution, tail latencies, throughput, DB size/fragmentation, read/write operation rates, and fleet-wide comparison.

**Complements** `etcd-availability.json` (fleet SLO violators) and `per-cluster-drill-in.json` (single-cluster P99). This dashboard adds:
- Full latency distribution heatmaps (WAL fsync + backend commit)
- Tail latency percentiles (P99, P99.9, P99.99)
- Fsync operation rate (ops/sec) and latency vs throughput correlation
- DB size, in-use size, fragmentation %, quota usage
- Read/write/delete operation rates and slow request tracking
- Per-pod breakdown for noisy-neighbor detection
- Fleet-wide per-cluster comparison

**SLO targets:** WAL fsync P99 < 10ms, backend commit P99 < 25ms.

panels.description: Current WAL fsync P99 for the selected HCP namespace
panels.title: WAL Fsync P99

panels.description: Current WAL fsync P99.9 for the selected HCP namespace — catches intermittent disk stalls invisible at P99
panels.title: WAL Fsync P99.9

panels.description: Current backend commit P99 for the selected HCP namespace
panels.title: Backend Commit P99

panels.description: Current fsync operation rate (ops/sec) for the selected HCP namespace
panels.title: WAL Fsync Rate

panels.description: Heatmap of WAL fsync latency distribution over time. Shows the full shape of the latency distribution — not just P99. Dense bands at high latencies indicate sustained disk pressure, while sparse outliers indicate intermittent stalls.
panels.title: WAL Fsync Latency Heatmap

panels.description: Heatmap of backend commit latency distribution over time. Backend commits are larger than WAL fsyncs and have a higher SLO threshold (25ms vs 10ms).
panels.title: Backend Commit Latency Heatmap

panels.description: WAL fsync tail latency percentiles over time (P50, P90, P99, P99.9, P99.99). Divergence between P99 and P99.9/P99.99 indicates intermittent disk stalls that P99-only monitoring misses.
panels.title: WAL Fsync Tail Latencies (P50 → P99.99)

panels.description: Backend commit tail latency percentiles over time (P50, P90, P99, P99.9, P99.99). SLO threshold at 25ms.
panels.title: Backend Commit Tail Latencies (P50 → P99.99)

panels.description: WAL fsync and backend commit operation rates over time. High throughput combined with high latency indicates sustained disk pressure rather than intermittent stalls.
panels.title: Fsync Operation Rate

panels.description: WAL fsync P99 latency overlaid with fsync operation rate. When latency rises with constant throughput, the disk is degrading. When both rise together, the workload is increasing.
panels.title: Latency vs Throughput Correlation

panels.description: WAL fsync P99 latency per cluster across the fleet. Each line represents one cluster's P99. Quickly identify which clusters have disk-related latency issues.
panels.title: WAL Fsync P99 per Cluster (Fleet)

panels.description: Backend commit P99 latency per cluster across the fleet. Identifies clusters with slow disk commit performance.
panels.title: Backend Commit P99 per Cluster (Fleet)

panels.description: WAL fsync P99 per etcd pod in the selected HCP namespace. Asymmetry between pods may indicate a node-local disk issue rather than a fleet-wide problem.
panels.title: WAL Fsync P99 per etcd Pod

panels.description: Fsync operation rate per etcd pod. Uneven distribution may indicate leader imbalance or asymmetric write load.
panels.title: Fsync Rate per etcd Pod
DB Size & Health — Scenarios 2 (Helm bloat), 4 (Job garbage), 5 (High-cardinality CRs), 9 (No defrag)

panels.description: Current etcd DB total allocated size. Approaches 8 GB hard quota.
panels.title: DB Total Size

panels.description: Actual data in DB (excludes fragmented space). Compare with total size to detect fragmentation.
panels.title: DB In-Use Size

panels.description: Percentage of DB allocated to fragmented (wasted) space. High fragmentation means defrag is needed. >40% is critical.
panels.title: DB Fragmentation

panels.description: DB size as % of the 8 GB quota. At 100% the cluster goes read-only (NOSPACE alarm). SRE alert fires at 80%.
panels.title: DB % of Quota

panels.description: Current key-value put operation rate. High put rate combined with high WAL fsync latency indicates write saturation.
panels.title: Put Rate (ops/sec)

panels.description: DB growth over time. When total size approaches quota (8 GB default), etcd will trigger NOSPACE and go read-only. Gap between total and in-use indicates fragmented space needing defrag.
panels.title: DB Total Size, In-Use Size & Quota

panels.description: Rising fragmentation after compaction without defrag. Run `etcdctl defrag` when this exceeds 30%.
panels.title: DB Fragmentation Ratio Over Time
Read & Write Operation Rate — Scenario 8 (Abusive LIST clients)

panels.description: Range read rate vs put rate. Abusive LIST clients show massive range read spike with low put rate — this is pure read pressure, not write pressure. High range reads also cause backend commit latency spikes.
panels.title: Key Operation Rate (Reads vs Writes)

panels.description: Requests exceeding 300ms usually indicate disk pressure or network issues. Leader changes (election count rate) indicate instability.
panels.title: Slow Requests (>300ms) & Leader Changes
